title: Cohomological Hall Algebras and Quiver Correspondences

items.title: Affine quotients by products of general linear groups are algebraic stacks

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebraic Stacks, §§94.10–94.12
references.locator: Definition 94.12.1 and the action-groupoid presentation criterion in §§94.10–94.11

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Groups, corrected 2022 printing, §2.8
references.locator: Printed pp. 40–41 (PDF pp. 51–52), the affine smooth group scheme GL_n

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be an affine finite-type
$\mathbb C$-scheme with an algebraic action of
$G=\prod_{r=1}^m\operatorname{GL}_{n_r,\mathbb C}$, allowing $n_r=0$.
Then the quotient stack $[X/G]$, defined by $G$-torsors with equivariant
maps to $X$, is an algebraic stack. The morphism $X\to[X/G]$ from the
trivial torsor is a smooth surjective representable atlas, and the diagonal
of $[X/G]$ is representable by affine schemes.

items.title: Representation stacks and exact-sequence correspondences of a finite quiver

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §2.1–2.2
Dominic Joyce, Cohomological Hall Algebras, Week 2 notes, Geometry Advanced Class Trinity Term 2026, §§1–2

items.statement:
Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver, in the convention of
[[def-path-ring-of-a-finite-quiver-over-the-integers]], and work over
$\mathbb C$. A **dimension vector** is a function
$\mathbf d:Q_0\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. Put
$
V_i^{\mathbf d}=\mathbb C^{d_i},\qquad
\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)=
\bigoplus_{h:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}
(V_i^{\mathbf d},V_j^{\mathbf d}),\qquad
G_{\mathbf d}=\prod_{i\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}(V_i^{\mathbf d}).
$
The group acts by change of basis:
$(g\cdot X)_h=g_jX_hg_i^{-1}$. The **representation stack**
$\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)/G_{\mathbf d}]$
is the quotient stack: over a scheme $T$, its objects are left
$G_{\mathbf d}$-torsors $P\to T$ with equivariant maps
$P\to\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$;
arrows are equivariant isomorphisms commuting with these maps. The
finite-dimensional atlas and the algebraic-stack conditions are verified in
[[lem-general-linear-quotient-stacks-are-algebraic]].

For two dimension vectors $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$, write
$\mathbf d=\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and choose
$V_i^{\mathbf d}=V_i^{\mathbf a}\oplus V_i^{\mathbf b}$. Let
$\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ be the vector space of
representations preserving $V^{\mathbf a}$. For an arrow $h:i\to j$, its
matrix has the form
$
X_h=
\begin{pmatrix}
X_h^{\mathbf a}&C_h\\
0&X_h^{\mathbf b}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad C_h\in\operatorname{Hom}(V_i^{\mathbf b},V_j^{\mathbf a}).
$
Let $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\subseteq G_{\mathbf d}$ be the subgroup preserving
the chosen graded subspaces. Define the **exact-sequence stack**
$
\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)/P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}].
$
Its maps are
$
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
\xleftarrow{\ q\ }\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
\xrightarrow{\ p\ }\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}.
$
The map $q$ sends an exact sequence to its subrepresentation and quotient;
$p$ forgets the subrepresentation. Thus the order convention is
$0\to M_{\mathbf a}\to M_{\mathbf d}\to M_{\mathbf b}\to0$.
The block form shows that the off-diagonal extension parameters are the
coordinates $C_h$; it does not assert that extension classes are a vector
space after quotienting by automorphisms.

~~~tikzcd
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
& \mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
  \arrow[l,"q"'] \arrow[r,"p"]
& \mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}
~~~

The diagram records only the two maps just defined; it supplies no equality of
maps or algebraic operation by itself.

items.title: The quiver exact-sequence correspondence is smooth and proper

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §2.2
Dominic Joyce, Cohomological Hall Algebras, Week 2 notes, Geometry Advanced Class Trinity Term 2026, §2.1

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $Q$ be a finite quiver and let $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$ be
dimension vectors. In the notation of
[[def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exact-sequence-correspondences]], the
map $q:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}$ is a smooth morphism of
algebraic stacks of relative complex dimension
$
r_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)
=\sum_{h:i\to j} b_i a_j-\sum_{i\in Q_0}a_i b_i
=-\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a),
$
where
$
\chi_Q(\mathbf u,\mathbf v)
=\sum_i u_i v_i-\sum_{h:i\to j}u_i v_j.
$
The forgetful map $p:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$ is representable and proper. These claims
allow loops, multiple arrows, zero coordinates, and the empty quiver.

items.title: Quiver potentials and on-shell monodromic coefficient data

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §§4.7 and 7.4–7.6
Ben Davison, The critical CoHA of a quiver with potential, §§2.2–2.7 and 3.1–3.2
Yan Soibelman, Remarks on Cohomological Hall algebras and their representations, §§2.1 and 2.4

items.statement:
Assume AC as inherited from the equivariant constructible category. Let $Q$
be a finite quiver. A **quiver potential** is a finite
$\mathbb C$-linear combination of directed cycles in the path algebra
$\mathbb C Q=\mathbb C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb ZQ$, modulo cyclic
rotation of each cycle. For a cycle
$h_1:i_0\to i_1,\ldots,h_\ell:i_{\ell-1}\to i_0$ and a representation
$X\in\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$, its trace is
$\operatorname{tr}(X_{h_\ell}\cdots X_{h_1})$. Extending linearly defines
the regular function $W_{\mathbf d}$ on $\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$.

This formula is well-defined modulo cyclic rotation. For linear maps
$A:U\to V$ and $B:V\to U$, the matrix-entry formula gives
$\operatorname{tr}_V(AB)=\sum_{v,u}A_{vu}B_{uv}=\sum_{u,v}B_{uv}A_{vu}=\operatorname{tr}_U(BA)$. Taking $A$ to be the first arrow map of a cycle and $B$ the product of its remaining arrow maps proves that moving the first arrow to the end leaves the trace unchanged. Under a change of vertex bases $(g_i)$, the product around a cycle based at $i_0$ changes to $g_{i_0}(X_{h_\ell}\cdots X_{h_1})g_{i_0}^{-1}$, whose trace is unchanged by the same identity. Thus $W_{\mathbf d}$ is $G_{\mathbf d}$-invariant and descends to the representation stack; differentiating this invariance shows that its critical locus is $G_{\mathbf d}$-stable.

Its critical locus $\operatorname{Crit}(W_{\mathbf d})$ is the zero scheme of the differential $dW_{\mathbf d}$.

The following is the **on-shell monodromic coefficient datum** used for a
conditional critical CoHA. For each $\mathbf d$, choose a set
$S_{\mathbf d}\subseteq\mathbb C$ containing the critical values of
$W_{\mathbf d}$, and require $S_{\mathbf a}+S_{\mathbf b}\subseteq
S_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$ for every pair of dimension vectors. One may always
take $S_{\mathbf d}=\mathbb C$; coefficients supported on an empty critical
fiber are zero. For each $z\in S_{\mathbf d}$, supply a bounded
$G_{\mathbf d}$-equivariant constructible complex $\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}$
supported on
$\operatorname{Crit}(W_{\mathbf d})\cap W_{\mathbf d}^{-1}(z)$, together
with a specified monodromy automorphism. Here **monodromic** means a complex
together with that chosen automorphism. At an isolated critical point, the
chosen normalization identifies its stalk with the reduced cohomology of the
local Milnor fiber, with $\widetilde H^0$ in degree zero; monodromy is
continuation around a positive loop about $z$.

The datum also specifies its coefficient category, complex-orientation shifts,
and the following operations for the exact-sequence correspondences:

1. proper pushforward along $p$ and smooth pullback along $q$;
2. an external-product (Thom–Sebastiani) isomorphism from the coefficients
   for $(\mathbf a,z_1)$ and $(\mathbf b,z_2)$ to the coefficient on the
   extension correspondence for $(\mathbf a+\mathbf b,z_1+z_2)$;
3. associativity and unit coherence of the iterated external products, and
   compatibility of all these maps with composition and proper/smooth base
   change;
4. the coefficient $\mathbb Q$ in dimension zero with its identity unit.

These clauses define the input data and required interface; they do not assert
that a canonical vanishing-cycle theory supplies it. The usual critical
vanishing-cycle complexes in monodromic mixed Hodge modules are an intended
instance, but their equivariant functoriality, orientation, and
Thom–Sebastiani compatibility are not proved by this Definition. Off-shell
rapid-decay cohomology is a different construction and is not included here.

items.title: Source-reported preprojective CoHA actions and their type boundaries

references.title: Yaping Yang and Gufang Zhao, The cohomological Hall algebra of a preprojective algebra, §§0.1–0.4, 5.1–5.6, and 7–8
Hiraku Nakajima, Introduction to quiver varieties—for ring and representation theorists, §§2–4

items.statement:
For a finite quiver \(Q\), its **double** adds an opposite arrow \(h^*\) for
each arrow \(h\). The **preprojective algebra** is the path algebra of the
double modulo the vertex moment-map relations
\(\sum_{h:\,t(h)=i}\epsilon(h)B_hB_{h^*}=0\), with the sign fixed by an
orientation of the original arrows. A **framed Nakajima variety**
\(\mathfrak M(\mathbf v,\mathbf w)\) is the geometric quotient of the
stable locus of framed doubled-quiver representations satisfying the
corresponding moment-map equation; stability \(\theta^+\), framing dimensions
\(\mathbf w\), and the cohomology theory are part of the input.

Yang–Zhao report that for a finite quiver and an algebraic oriented cohomology
theory \(A\) with the formal-group-law and torus-action hypotheses in their
§§1.1 and 3.1, the preprojective CoHA
\[
P_A(Q)=\bigoplus_{\mathbf v}
A^*_{G_{\mathbf v}\times\mathbb G_m^2}
(\mu_{\mathbf v}^{-1}(0))
\]
is associative and acts on the \(A\)-homology of
\(\mathfrak M(\mathbf v,\mathbf w)\) with the fixed positive stability
\(\theta^+\) (their Theorems A and B). This action statement is for arbitrary
finite \(Q\) in their stated setup.

Their Yangian comparison is a narrower result. With Chow theory, no edge
loops, the Euler–Ringel sign twist
\[
\widetilde m_{\mathbf v_1,\mathbf v_2}
=(-1)^{(\mathbf v_2,C\mathbf v_1)+1}m_{\mathbf v_1,\mathbf v_2},
\qquad C=I-A_D,
\]
the spherical extension, specialization \(t_1=t_2=\hbar/2\), and quotient by
the specified torsion, Yang–Zhao prove a surjection from the positive Borel
of the quiver Yangian; it is an isomorphism for simply-laced ADE quivers, and
the isomorphism intertwines the stated Nakajima-variety action (Theorems D
and 8.3). Here ADE means the underlying graph is a finite Dynkin diagram of
type \(A,D,\) or \(E\). The Yangian is the algebra defined in their §8.

Nakajima’s ordinary Kac–Moody action uses a finite quiver with no edge loops.
It acts on the Borel–Moore homology of the Lagrangian core of the framed
quiver variety and gives an integrable highest-weight representation with
highest weight \(\mathbf w\) (Theorem 17 of the review, referring to the
original papers). The review omits the geometric proof of the Lagrangian
theorem and refers the action relations to those original papers.

These are source reports with their stated conventions and hypotheses. This
Remark supplies no local action theorem, Yangian comparison, or logical
supplier; no general CoHA–Yangian identification follows from the untwisted
associativity theorem.

items.title: The untwisted equivariant Borel–Moore CoHA of a finite quiver

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §§2.1–2.3
Dominic Joyce, Cohomological Hall Algebras, Week 2 notes, Geometry Advanced Class Trinity Term 2026, §§1–2
Yan Soibelman, Remarks on Cohomological Hall algebras and their representations, §2.2

items.statement:
Assume AC as inherited from the equivariant Borel–Moore supplier. Let $Q$
be a finite quiver over $\mathbb C$. Use rational equivariant
Borel–Moore homology with the complex orientation and normalization of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. The
untwisted quiver CoHA module is the dimension-vector graded direct sum
$
\mathcal H_Q=\bigoplus_{\mathbf d\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{Q_0}}
H_*^{\mathrm{BM},G_{\mathbf d}}
(\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d);\mathbb Q).
$
This is an algebraic direct sum; no completion is used.

For $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$, let
$q:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}$ and
$p:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$
be the maps of
[[def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exact-sequence-correspondences]].
The product of $\alpha$ in dimension $\mathbf a$ and $\beta$ in
dimension $\mathbf b$ is
$
\alpha*\beta:=p_*q^!(\alpha\boxtimes\beta),
$
where $\boxtimes$ is the equivariant external product,
$q^!$ is the smooth complex-oriented Borel–Moore pullback, and $p_*$ is
the proper pushforward. By
[[lem-quiver-exact-sequence-correspondence-is-smooth-and-proper]], the
homological degree changes by
$
2r_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a),
\qquad
\chi_Q(\mathbf u,\mathbf v)=
\sum_i u_i v_i-\sum_{h:i\to j}u_i v_j.
$
Thus the first factor is the subrepresentation and the second is the
quotient. This normalization has no Euler-form sign twist, no division by
automorphism orders, and no additional Tate twist. Each dimension vector has
only finitely many decompositions into $\mathbf a+\mathbf b$, so the product
on the direct sum is defined.

The zero dimension component is $\mathbb Q$; write $1$ for its
standard class, the candidate unit.

The displayed homological shift is for this Borel–Moore normalization and the
subrepresentation-first convention. Under the usual equivariant cohomology
grading, converting through the quotient-stack dimensions gives the source
shift $-2\chi_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$; it is not obtained by simply
reversing the arguments in the displayed Borel–Moore formula.

**Unresolved operation interface.** The formula uses Borel–Moore pullback and
pushforward for maps of quotient stacks. The cited Borel–Moore item defines
these operations for equivariant correspondences of schemes with a fixed
acting group; it does not supply the required change from the block-parabolic
group $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}$ to its Levi group
$G_{\mathbf a}\times G_{\mathbf b}$, or the push to
$G_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$. This definition records the intended product,
but its well-definedness in the declared model remains escalated.

items.title: A quiver potential trace is additive on exact sequences

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §4.7
Ben Davison, The critical CoHA of a quiver with potential, §3.1

items.statement:
Let $W$ be a potential of a finite quiver $Q$, and let
$0\to M_{\mathbf a}\to M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}\to M_{\mathbf b}\to0$
be represented by a point of the exact-sequence stack. Then
$
W_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}(M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b})
=W_{\mathbf a}(M_{\mathbf a})+W_{\mathbf b}(M_{\mathbf b}).
$

items.title: The untwisted quiver CoHA is associative and unital

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §2.3
Dominic Joyce, Cohomological Hall Algebras, Week 2 notes, Geometry Advanced Class Trinity Term 2026, §§2.1–2.2
Yan Soibelman, Remarks on Cohomological Hall algebras and their representations, §2.2

items.statement:
Assume AC as inherited from the equivariant Borel–Moore and six-functor
suppliers. For every finite quiver $Q$, the multiplication in
[[def-untwisted-quiver-cohomological-hall-algebra]] is associative and has unit
the class $1\in H_0^{\mathrm{BM}}(\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf 0);\mathbb Q)
=\mathbb Q$.

items.title: A conditional critical CoHA from monodromic vanishing-cycle data

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §§4.7 and 7.4–7.6
Ben Davison, The critical CoHA of a quiver with potential, §§2.2–2.7 and 3.1–3.2
Yan Soibelman, Remarks on Cohomological Hall algebras and their representations, §§2.1 and 2.4

items.statement:
Assume AC as inherited from the equivariant Borel–Moore and constructible
categories. Let $Q,W$ be as in
[[def-quiver-potential-and-monodromic-vanishing-cycle-data]], and suppose a
monodromic coefficient datum $\mathscr V$ satisfying all four clauses of
that Definition has been supplied. For a dimension vector $\mathbf d$ and
$z\in S_{\mathbf d}$, define homology with coefficients in
$\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}$ by
$
H_n^{\mathrm{BM},G_{\mathbf d}}
(\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d);\Phi_{\mathbf d,z})
:=\mathbb H^{-n}_{G_{\mathbf d}}
(\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d),
\omega_{\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)}^{G_{\mathbf d}}
\otimes^{\mathbb L}\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}).
$
The **conditional critical CoHA** is the direct sum
$
\mathcal H^{\mathrm{crit}}_{Q,W,\mathscr V}
=\bigoplus_{\mathbf d}\ \bigoplus_{z\in S_{\mathbf d}}
H_*^{\mathrm{BM},G_{\mathbf d}}
(\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d);\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}).
$
For $z_1\in S_{\mathbf a}$ and $z_2\in S_{\mathbf b}$, multiply by
$p_*q^!$ using the proper, smooth, and external-product maps in
$\mathscr V$; its output lies in value $z_1+z_2$. The degree shift is
$-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$, the same Borel–Moore convention as in
[[def-untwisted-quiver-cohomological-hall-algebra]]. Finite sums of
dimension/value-supported inputs multiply to finite sums, so this direct-sum
algebraic structure needs no completion.

This is the on-shell construction with monodromy retained. It is not the
off-shell rapid-decay realization, and it asserts no existence theorem for a
standard mixed-Hodge-module or 3-Calabi–Yau orientation package.

This construction also uses the quotient-stack Borel–Moore operation
interface required by
[[def-untwisted-quiver-cohomological-hall-algebra]]. That interface is not
supplied by the current fixed-group equivariant Borel–Moore item, so the
critical CoHA definition remains escalated until that prerequisite is
established.

items.title: Critical quiver CoHA multiplication is associative under its coherence axioms

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §§2.3 and 7.6
Ben Davison, The critical CoHA of a quiver with potential, §§2.5–2.7 and 3.2

items.statement:
Assume AC as inherited from the equivariant Borel–Moore and coefficient
categories. Let $Q,W$ be as above and let $\mathscr V$ be any on-shell monodromic
coefficient datum satisfying all clauses in
[[def-quiver-potential-and-monodromic-vanishing-cycle-data]]. Then the
multiplication of
[[def-critical-quiver-coha-from-vanishing-cycle-data]] is associative and
unital.

title: Cohomological Hall Algebras and Quiver Correspondences: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The one-loop quiver extension correspondence in dimension two

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §2.5
Dominic Joyce, Cohomological Hall Algebras, Week 2 notes, Geometry Advanced Class Trinity Term 2026, §4.1

items.statement:
Let $Q$ have one vertex and one loop $x$:

~~~tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[>=stealth]
  \node[circle,draw,inner sep=2.5pt] (v) at (0,0) {$\bullet$};
  \draw[->] (v) edge[loop above] node {$x$} (v);
\end{tikzpicture}
~~~

Take $\mathbf a=\mathbf b=1$. Then
$\operatorname{Rep}_Q(1)=\mathbb C$ and
$\operatorname{Rep}_Q(2)=\operatorname{Mat}_2(\mathbb C)$. The group
$\operatorname{GL}_1$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{Rep}_Q(1)$, while
$\operatorname{GL}_2$ acts on $\operatorname{Rep}_Q(2)$ by conjugation.
The extension atlas consists of pairs $(A,L)$ with $L$ a line in
$\mathbb C^2$ and $A(L)\subseteq L$. In a basis adapted to $L$,
$
A=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&c\\0&\mu\end{pmatrix}.
$
The map $q$ records the scalars $(\lambda,\mu)$, and the map $p$ forgets
$L$.

items.title: The trace potential x squared on the one-loop quiver

references.title: Maxim Kontsevich and Yan Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson-Thomas invariants, §4.7
Ben Davison, The critical CoHA of a quiver with potential, §6.1
Yan Soibelman, Remarks on Cohomological Hall algebras and their representations, §2.4

items.statement:
For the one-vertex, one-loop quiver with loop $x$, take the potential
$W=x^2$. In dimension one, the representation space is $\mathbb C$, the
group $\operatorname{GL}_1$ acts trivially, and the trace function is
$W_1(z)=z^2$. Its critical locus is the origin, with critical value zero.
